title: 2.4.33 Challenges: Stretch Problems
description: Stretch problems. Every challenge is required to continue. Auto-graded.
sourceRef: designed: stretch bundle for §2.4 Loop Control and Nested Loops

steps.title: Hollow square
steps.instructions: Print a 6x6 hollow square using nested loops: a "#" on the border rows and border columns, and a space everywhere else inside.

steps.title: Sum every third number
steps.instructions: Loop through the integers 1 to 50. Using continue, skip every number that is NOT a multiple of 3. Add up the ones you keep and log the total.

steps.title: Multiplication table, skip multiples of 5
steps.instructions: Print a multiplication table for 1 to 12 using a nested loop, one row per outer number. Use continue to skip printing any row whose outer number is a multiple of 5.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "2.4.33 Challenges: Stretch Problems". The task they were given: Print a 6x6 hollow square using nested loops: a "#" on the border rows and border columns, and a space everywhere else inside. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
